Cc: support@finrise.com
Date: 2026-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production latency & 5xx — reserved throughput not meeting committed QPS

Olga —

We started seeing a sustained latency spike and ~3% 5xx rate on our inference route (model: rwinf-7b) starting ~08:58 PDT. Our logs show queueing and token-throttle responses indicating the reserved throughput for our Dedicated pool is not being honored — despite our 10k QPS reservation. This is impacting checkout flows and is currently hitting our SRE team's alerting.

We need an immediate mitigation. Can you confirm whether this is a quirk in routing, a pool saturation event, or something else? We attach a small sample of logs and a timeline. Also flagging procurement@finrise.com — if this continues through our weekend our renewal/penalty conversation will be immediate.

Attaching: inference_logs_sample.csv (sent via separate upload)

Amit Shah
SRE Lead, FinRise

Amit — thank you for the heads-up and the log sample. We're on it. Immediate notes:

- I’ve opened an incident (INC-2026-8421) and alerted on-call infra.
- Preliminary telemetry shows a sudden rise in active tokens and a matching drop in per-tenant scheduling headroom for the Dedicated GPU pool that backs your reservation.
- I’m activating a short-term aisle: enable emergency burst capacity (best-effort), and switch your traffic to the fallback routing policy to reduce head-of-line queueing while we triage.

Can you confirm a good time for a 20-minute bridge now (15–20 min)? If you can share a fuller log bundle (full inference_logs.zip) that will speed root cause.

I’ve CC'd engineering and customer success to coordinate credits and an exec readout if needed.

Date: 2026-08-14T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency & 5xx — reserved throughput not meeting committed QPS

Olga / team — quick findings from the first 20 minutes of debug (dropping raw traces to thread):

- Symptom: sustained token queue depth growth on the serving runtime for pool-ded-14 that matches FinRise's tenant ID. Observed sudden increase in long-context requests from another tenant (~50% extra tokens) at 08:55 PDT.
- Root-cause hypothesis: cross-tenant spillover due to mis-tagged routing group that allowed bursty traffic to bypass isolation heuristics. The scheduler then applied contention and FIFO behavior for the affected LLM instances, starving reserved lanes.
- Immediate mitigation applied:
  1) Manual tag-enforcement to isolate FinRise tenancy (completed 09:34).
  2) Enabled emergency burst (up to 2x for 15 minutes) to drain backlog (in progress).
  3) Switched FinRise route to 'latency-first' fallback — reduces batching for quick tokens.

Action items for approvals: we need Exec sign-off to keep burst enabled for next 6 hours (uses reserved burst budget). Also recommend offering FinRise a short invoice credit pending postmortem.

Marissa
Director, Reliability Engineering
